decisionsTitle: A volunteer's type — «Tip» on the «Voluntari» list, and the role's category on its badge
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17, on a phone, four days before Saturday's race (2026-11-21):** «Practic voluntarii sunt de 2 tipuri: start-finish și pe traseu». Then, with a picture of the «Voluntari» list, whose «Roluri date» read «foto/video (Activități start/finish), foto/video (Pe Traseu)» and «direcționare (Activități start/finish)»: «și pe ecuson vreau, și în tabelul ăsta». Asked what exactly, he chose: **the type — start–finish or route — taken from the category of the role given; on the badge beside the role, and in the list a new column «Tip»**. Amends §774, which kept the badge's band to the role alone and refused «showing the category on the badge's band», and §764 (what a badge prints); adds a column to the list of §839.

**Decision — the type is the category of the roles given, and nothing new is stored.** The club already named its two types: an event's roles sit under the club's own categories (§774) — for Saturday's race «Activități start/finish» and «Pe Traseu» — and a volunteer's roles are the ones the organizers gave (`event_volunteer_role_assignments`, §837). So a person's type is the category of each role given, in the club's words: no column, no setting, no migration, and a club whose categories are something else sees its own words. A role under no category has no type: its default heading «Alte activități» is a heading of the card, never printed as a type.

- **«Tip» on the «Voluntari» list.** A column right after «Roluri date» and before «Punct», headed «Tip» / “Type” with its «?» (where the person works, from the category of the roles given; empty when no role is given or none has a category; where the categories are written). The cell names the categories of the roles **given** — never of the roles only offered — in the page's language, each once, in the order the club set the categories (`sort`, then age, as `compareCategories`), joined by «, »: «Activități start/finish», or «Activități start/finish, Pe Traseu» for someone given a role in each. Nobody given a role, or only roles under none: an empty cell, and no line on a phone's card (`omitEmptyOnPhone`). A cancelled person who still holds roles shows their type, as «Roluri date» shows their roles. It is read in the page's one read of the roles' words (`listRoleNames`, which now also carries each category's place in the club's order), never a query per row, and ordered by the pure `volunteerTypes`. For everyone who sees the list today nothing else changes: no sort, no filter, no verb.
- **The badge.** A role's badge (the design's «Câte un ecuson pe rol») prints the name of the role's category — in the badge's language and in the small line's own capitals — after «VOLUNTAR» on the small line above the role's name: «VOLUNTAR · PE TRASEU», «VOLUNTEER · ON THE ROUTE»; the club's own word first when it typed one, « · » between them, no word of the platform's. **Measured, not guessed** (the bib's font tables, the measure every badge line is fitted by): the small line shrinks down to its least size — 6 pt on the two strips (5.3 pt when the free-text line and the telephone both squeeze the bands), 5.3 pt on the smallest badge the designer accepts, 60 × 30 mm. «VOLUNTAR · ACTIVITĂȚI START/FINISH» is 18.3 em and «VOLUNTAR · PE TRASEU» 11.2 em, so both of Saturday's categories stand beside «VOLUNTAR» on every size the designer accepts — at the very size «VOLUNTAR» has alone on the two strips and on the smallest badge (97 pt of the 152 pt band at 60 × 30 mm), the line shrinking on a tall, narrow badge as any line too wide for its room does. But «VOLUNTAR · » and an 80-character name — the longest the categories' editor keeps — need 258 to 456 pt at that least size (an 80-letter Romanian name 48.6 em, eighty «W» 76 em), while the band is 151.6 pt wide at 60 × 30 mm and 235.2 pt on the default 90 × 35 mm. The line above cannot hold the longest name at the smallest size the design allows, so the choice is made **per badge, by that measure**: the line above whenever the category fits there at that line's least size, shrunk as «VOLUNTAR» alone is shrunk; otherwise «VOLUNTAR» stays alone and the category takes **a small line of its own under the role's name**, at most the small line's size, shrunk until it fits and never cut (`badgeFitWhole`: past its half-point steps it fills the width exactly), the role's name giving up what three lines need of the band's height but never going below its own least size (6 pt), so a role's name is cut only where it was cut before. On the default strip an 80-letter Romanian name prints at 5.3 pt under a 10.8 pt role name; eighty wide capitals, or eighty «ß» (160 capitals once uppercased), print whole and very small.
- **Every size still fits everything it shows.** The category's line stands inside the role's band whichever line it takes: it adds no row, so the header, the band, the free-text line, the writing area and the telephone keep their heights, and the save's fit check (`badgeSizeRefusal`, `BADGE_SIZE_TOO_SMALL`), which reads those rows, answers as before — no size the designer accepts needs refusing now. Tested at every width step and every whole height the bounds allow, with every tick, for three 80-character names: whole, inside the band's width and height, no line over another, the rows unchanged, the role's name never under its least size; and at the smallest sizes accepted, 60 × 30 mm and, with the free-text line and the telephone, 60 × 34 mm.
- **One source.** The sheet (`badges-pdf.ts`), the picture (`badge-image.tsx` through the preview route) and the print panel's pictures draw the same layout from the same words: `badgeRoleFace` hands a role to the print's piles and to the preview route alike, `badgeLayoutWords` builds the words both renderers lay out, `badgeLayout` places the lines. The sheet's layout cache is keyed by the category too, so «Direcționare» under two categories prints as two badges. The pictures are stamped with the category's names in both languages — a category renamed is a new picture — and `BADGE_DRAWING_VERSION` is 2.
- **What prints as before.** A role under no category, a badge «fără rol» and the one badge for everyone (§783) print exactly what they printed: each is held to its drawing written from the code before the change — the layout, the picture's markup and every call made to pdfkit (`tests/unit/volunteers/badge-type-unchanged.test.ts`). The designer's help under «Cuvântul de pe bandă» now says that on the badges per role the category goes with «VOLUNTAR».

**Not done (each its own change, when asked).** A filter or a sort by type on the list; the type on «Planul voluntarilor», on the person's page, in the volunteers' Excel and CSV, in the emails and on the public volunteers' form or list; a type stored on a person, or set on a role apart from its category; a tick to keep the category off the badge. The categories' editor, the registrations and the files are unchanged.

**Refused.** A new setting or column for the type: the club's categories already say it, in its own words. Refusing a badge size because a category could be long: the design is saved apart from the categories, which are typed later in another card, so a size would be refused for a name nobody wrote — the line shrinks inside the band instead. Wrapping a long category onto two lines: it would take the height the role's name needs on every small badge, for names no club types. Cutting a long category with «…», as the free-text line is cut: the type is what the line is for.
changelogLine: - **A volunteer's type, on the list and on the badge** — the «Voluntari» list has a column «Tip» naming the categories of the roles given to each person, and a role's badge prints its category beside «VOLUNTAR» («VOLUNTAR · PE TRASEU»), or on a small line under the role's name when it is too long for that line; badges with no category print as before. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the «Voluntari» list, then a column «Tip» / “Type” with its «?» stands right after «Roluri date» and before «Punct»; its cell names, in the page's language, the categories of the roles given to the person — never of the roles only offered — each once, in the order the club set the categories, joined by «, »; a role under no category adds nothing, and a person given no role, or only such roles, has an empty cell and no line on a phone's card; the column neither sorts nor filters, and the page reads it in the one read of the roles' words it already makes, never a query per row (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 158 (the badge's band prints the role only). Given a volunteer badge per role whose role sits under a category, then the badge prints the category's name in the badge's language and in the small line's capitals: after «VOLUNTAR» and « · » on the small line above the role's name when that line holds both at its least size, else on a small line of its own under the role's name, never larger than the small line and never cut; the role's name stays alone on the large line; the PDF, the picture and the print panel's picture print the same words at the same sizes, in Romanian and in English (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a volunteer badge for a role under no category, a badge «fără rol» or the one badge for everyone, then it prints exactly what it printed before a role's category reached the badge: the same layout, the same picture and the same calls to the PDF (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given any size the badge designer accepts, with any of its rows ticked, and a category name of 80 characters, the longest the event's editor keeps, then the category prints whole, inside the role's band and over no other line; the badge's rows, and so the save's answer to the size (`BADGE_SIZE_TOO_SMALL`), are the same as without it, and the role's name is never set under its least size nor cut where it was not cut before (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
